references.text: The fourth commandment concerning the Sabbath, which provides the basis for resting on the seventh day after six days of work.
Repeats the command to work six days and rest on the seventh, emphasizing the holiness of the Sabbath.
Parallel text commanding rest on the seventh day, even during plowing and harvest seasons.
Moses repeats the Sabbath commandment to the people of Israel, with six days of work and rest on the seventh.
The Sabbath commandment repeated in Deuteronomy, with special emphasis that servants, slaves, and foreigners must also rest.
The Sabbath commandment in the Holiness Code, which forbids work on the seventh day.
Nehemiah enforces Sabbath observance and prohibits trade on the Sabbath to protect the day of rest.
Isaiah speaks of the blessing of honoring the Sabbath and refraining from one's own pursuits on this holy day.
Ezekiel confirms that the Sabbath was given as a sign between God and Israel.
Jesus heals on the Sabbath and points out that people and animals need to be freed from burdens on the Sabbath.
Jesus teaches that the Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.
Expands and offers a deep theological exploration of the theme of giving rest to the oppressed by linking it to God's own Sabbath.
The direct parallel in the Ten Commandments confirming that Sabbath rest applies to all social classes without exception.
Creates a profound theological contrast by showing the consequence of refusing Sabbath rest: the land is forced to rest through desolation.
